intro: This unit visits two rooms. The first is the roda, the circle where capoeira is played in Brazil. The second is the boxing ring, a roped square that grew out of English prize fights. Both have music, rules or ceremonies that tell people when to begin and when to stop.

Both arts faced the law. Brazil's Penal Code of 1890 made capoeira a crime, two years after slavery ended. In England and America, bare-knuckle prize fights were often illegal until written rules, gloves and state commissions changed the sport. Schools, gyms, churches and governments each made choices about these arts.

By the end, you will be able to name the people who opened schools and wrote rules, such as Mestre Bimba, Mestre Pastinha and John Graham Chambers. You will read dates in order, from 1743 to 2014. You will explain how a gym, a school association and a heritage office each shape a martial art.
bigQuestion: How do laws, schools and rulebooks decide where a martial art is allowed to happen?

test.q: What is the roda in capoeira?
choices: the circle of people where capoeira is played
test.why: Roda is Portuguese for circle, the ring where the jogo happens.

test.q: In what year did Brazil end slavery?
test.why: Princess Isabel signed the Golden Law on May 13, 1888.

test.q: What did Brazil's Penal Code of 1890 do to capoeira?
choices: made it a crime in streets and squares
test.why: Article 402 made capoeira in public places a crime, with two to six months in prison.

test.q: Who led the first capoeira school recognized by the Bahia government?
test.why: Bahia registered Mestre Bimba's school in 1937.

test.q: Which style did Mestre Pastinha keep and teach?
test.why: Pastinha founded the Centro Esportivo de Capoeira Angola in Salvador in 1941.

choices: added the capoeira circle to its heritage list
test.why: In 2014, UNESCO added the capoeira circle to its list of intangible heritage.

test.q: Who wrote the first boxing rules in England, in 1743?
test.why: Jack Broughton posted his rules at his London amphitheatre in 1743.

test.q: How long is a round under the Queensberry Rules?
test.why: The Queensberry Rules set three-minute rounds with one minute of rest.

test.q: Why are the rules called the Queensberry Rules if Chambers wrote them?
choices: The Marquess of Queensberry supported them and lent his name.
test.why: Chambers wrote the rules; the Marquess of Queensberry backed them, so they carry his name.

test.q: What happened in the 1892 fight between Sullivan and Corbett?
choices: It was the last bare-knuckle title fight.
It was held at Soldier Field.
Corbett won the first heavyweight title under Queensberry Rules.
test.why: Corbett beat Sullivan in New Orleans in 1892, with gloves, under the Queensberry Rules.

choices: white champions refusing to fight Black boxers
test.why: White champions refused Black challengers until Jack Johnson won the title in 1908.

test.q: When did women's boxing join the Olympic Games?
test.why: Women first boxed at the Olympics in London in 2012.

test.q: Which group licenses professional boxers in a state?
test.why: A state athletic commission, like New York's from 1920, licenses professional fighters.

test.q: How are IPHAN in Brazil and the IHSA in Illinois alike?
choices: Both are official bodies that decide which activities they recognize.
test.why: IPHAN recognizes heritage and the IHSA decides school state finals; each is an official body.

test.q: What do a capoeira academy and a town boxing gym have in common?
choices: Both are places outside school teams where people learn an art.
Both are run by the IHSA.
test.why: Academies like Bimba's and gyms like the CYO's gave people places to learn outside school teams.

write.prompt: Capoeira and boxing were both once treated as problems by the law. Which art changed its place in society more, and why? Use at least three dates or documents from the unit, such as Article 402 (1890), Bimba's 1937 registration, the Queensberry Rules (1867) or the Walker Law (1920).
tips: Name each document or record and give its year.
Say who made each rule: a government, a club, a school group or a heritage office.
Compare the two arts side by side before you decide.
Use unit words like roda, penal code, commission and color line.
Name the people who were shut out and when doors opened.
